rationale: A wins because it mostly keeps its hands where the facts are: “Oatly's reformulated barista blend cuts climate footprint 31% per liter, verified by third-party LCA” is a clean reporter-shaped data angle with the right proof demands. B has sharper instincts in places, especially “What a 31% footprint cut actually measures — and what an LCA leaves out,” but then it starts selling facts it does not have: “default, not the upcharge” and “Someone is absorbing the difference.” That is how a useful angle set becomes a reporter correction waiting to happen.
gaps_in_A: “Oatly wins its biggest pour-volume deal” invents scale. The update says 1,400 locations, not that this is Oatly’s biggest deal or that pour volume is known.

“The retail angle: what no price change means for shoppers” is refused too quickly. No price change is weak alone, but paired with reformulation, losses, and plant closure it could support a margin/pricing question if handled carefully.
The customer angle’s “Facts it rests on” includes “no price change at retail,” which does not actually support a coffee-chain foodservice story. It is true, but it is stray proof.
The set could ask harder about the plant closure’s labor and capacity consequences; it flags plant identity and capacity, but not worker impact or timing.
gaps_in_B: “A 1,400-store coffee chain makes oat milk the default, not the upcharge” overclaims. The update says default non-dairy option; it says nothing about upcharges at the chain.

“Oatly reformulated and held the price. Someone is absorbing the difference.” assumes there is a cost difference to absorb. The update gives no input-cost direction, margin effect, or foodservice pricing.

“unprofitable plant-based companies retreat from sustainability spending when they cut costs” is a tidy contrarian setup, but it is not grounded in the supplied facts. It needs evidence or it needs to be cut.
“the kind of reporter who has been writing ‘the plant-based boom is over’ stories” leans on an external trend the update did not supply. Fine as later targeting research; lazy as angle grounding.
